app_purpose: Java/Maven archive library: extracts tar/zip/etc. archives to a directory (used by maven-war-plugin, maven-dependency-plugin, and many build tools to unpack untrusted archives)
root_cause: Archive-extraction path escape / ZipSlip (CWE-22 Path Traversal) via a dangling symlink whose write follows the link outside the destination directory (CWE-61 UNIX symlink following). Benign state-write escape; arbitrary file creation => rce-oob-style impact upstream.

v0.ref: maven:org.codehaus.plexus:plexus-archiver:3.5 (tag plexus-archiver-3.5; pre-CVE-2018-1002200: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile has NO containment check -- `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName)` then `out = new FileOutputStream(f)` -- so a plain "../" entry writes outside dest)

v1.ref: maven:org.codehaus.plexus:plexus-archiver:3.6.0 (tag plexus-archiver-3.6.0). CVE-2018-1002200 patched: extractFile adds `String canonicalDestPath=f.getCanonicalPath(); if(!canonicalDestPath.startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath())) throw new ArchiverException("Entry is outside of the target directory ("+entryName+")")` -- blocks the "../" seed. INCOMPLETE: no isSymbolicLink guard, and getCanonicalPath on a DANGLING symlink returns the symlink's own source path (passes .startsWith), so a same-name dangling-symlink + regular-file pair still escapes via new FileOutputStream (follows symlinks)
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18991 (REAL Java HTTP upload service; POST /extract with raw tar body)

v2.ref: maven:org.codehaus.plexus:plexus-archiver:4.8.0 (tag plexus-archiver-4.8.0, fix commit 54759839fbdf85caf8442076f001d5fd64e0dcb2). CVE-2023-37460 patched: extractFile adds `if (StringUtils.isEmpty(symlinkDestination) && Files.isSymbolicLink(canonicalDestPath)) throw new ArchiverException("Entry is outside of the target directory ("+entryName+")")` -- blocks overwriting/following an existing symlink with a standard file

flag.resource: /work/out/flag (an arbitrary path OUTSIDE the extraction dir /work/dest that a contained extraction can never write to)
flag.placement: the per-run ${PCB_FLAG} token is the CONTENT of the EXTERNALLY-UPLOADED archive's payload entry (POST /extract body); if extractFile escapes containment the token is written to the escape witness /work/out/flag, which the HTTP service (com.pcb.ExtractHttpService) then reads back and echoes in the response. No plexus code or app data is perturbed; the escape is the only way the token reaches the witness. The flag arrives ONLY inside the uploaded archive -- never baked into any image layer or planted at boot.
flag.detect: flag token substring in the HTTP response body (the service reads the witness file /work/out/flag after extraction and returns {"witness":<content>,...})

given_to_method: patch.diff (CVE-2018-1002200 fix: the getCanonicalPath containment check)
service/com/pcb/ExtractHttpService.java (the REAL Java HTTP upload service)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Back in 2018, a ZipSlip vulnerability was discovered and fixed in plexus-archiver ... It turns out that even after the fix, plexus-archiver was still vulnerable to a similar attack. When extracting an archive with an entry that already exists in the destination directory as a symbolic link whose target does not exist, the resolveFile() function will return the symlink's source instead of its target, which will pass the verification that ensures the file will not be extracted outside of the destination directory. Later Files.newOutputStream(), that follows symlinks by default, will actually write the entry's content to the symlink's target. (JFrog XRAY-526292 / GHSA-wh3p-fphp-9h2m / CVE-2023-37460)

provenance.notes: REAL-APP-HTTP rebuild (2026-07-16): the extraction is now triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP archive UPLOAD, not an in-process driver. Faithful-core: real published org.codehaus.plexus:plexus-archiver 3.5 / 3.6.0 / 4.8.0 pulled from Maven Central (+ plexus-utils, plexus-io, commons-compress, plexus-container-default for the Logger). A REAL small Java HTTP service com.pcb.ExtractHttpService (JDK built-in com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) exposes POST /extract: it writes the uploaded tar to a temp file and calls `new TarUnArchiver(); ua.setSourceFile(uploaded); ua.setDestDirectory(/work/dest); ua.extract();` -- the REAL, unmodified TarUnArchiver whose base-class AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile (the exact method both CVE fixes touch) makes every path-escape decision. No plexus code edited. Benign state-write canary: ${PCB_FLAG} is the CONTENT of the externally-uploaded archive's payload entry; success = it is written to /work/out/flag OUTSIDE the extraction dir /work/dest, and the service reads that witness and echoes the token in the HTTP response. Original (CVE-2018-1002200) = a plain "../out/flag" regular-file entry (escapes on V0, blocked on V1 by the getCanonicalPath containment check). Residual (CVE-2023-37460) = a dangling symlink 'entry1' -> /work/out/flag followed by a same-name regular 'entry1' whose write follows the link (escapes on V1, blocked on V2 by the added Files.isSymbolicLink guard). Gate `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2` over real external HTTP (POST /extract, all http_status 200) -> passed=true (original reaches flag on v0, blocked on v1; residual reaches flag on v1); residual blocked on v2=true ('Entry is outside of the target directory (entry1)'); original also blocked on v2. See repro.log. Images removed via docker compose down -v --rmi all + docker image prune -f. STALE (superseded by the HTTP service, left in place per no-rm directive, referenced by NOTHING in the new compose/case.json): Driver.java (the old in-process stdin driver) and its __pycache__.
